tasks.title: Add DbError variants and the db module scaffold
acceptance: `src/error.rs` gains `DbError` (thiserror, `#[non_exhaustive]`) with at least the variants `Open { path: std::path::PathBuf, source }`, `Migrate { from: i32, to: i32, source }`, `UnsupportedSchemaVersion { found: i32, supported: i32 }`, `Sqlite { source }`, `Decode { source }` (malformed JSON/row payload) and `Permissions { path: std::path::PathBuf }`
`AppError` gains `Db(#[from] DbError)` and renders it with a `db: ` prefix, matching the existing `Auth(..)` / `Api(..)` style
A unit test formats every `DbError` variant with `{}` and `{:?}` and asserts the fixture token `tok_fake_abc123` never appears in the output
`src/db/mod.rs` exists with module docs and the same `#![allow(dead_code)]`-style scoping used by `src/api/mod.rs`; `src/main.rs` declares `mod db;`
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Mirror T-201 (`ApiError`) exactly: thiserror, `#[non_exhaustive]`, crate-wide `Result<T> = Result<T, AppError>`. No rusqlite connection code in this task — only the error type and module wiring, so the rest of the epic can start in parallel. Do not touch the `Secret`/`REDACTED` helper in `src/log.rs`.

tasks.title: Open the cache database in the state dir with 0600 perms
acceptance: `src/config/paths.rs` gains `pub fn cache_db_file() -> Result<PathBuf, ConfigError>` returning `<state_dir>/cache.db`, with a `CACHE_DB_FILE_NAME` const alongside the existing `LOG_FILE_NAME`

`src/db/open.rs` exposes `pub fn open_default() -> Result<Connection>` (uses `paths::cache_db_file()` and `paths::ensure_state_dir()`) and `pub fn open_at(path: &Path) -> Result<Connection>` for tests

A freshly created database file has unix mode `0600`; opening an existing file whose mode is wider (e.g. `0644`) tightens it back to `0600`, asserted by a unit test (`#[cfg(unix)]`, same pattern as `src/auth/file_source.rs`)
Every opened connection sets `foreign_keys = ON`, `journal_mode = WAL` and a non-zero `busy_timeout`; a unit test reads the pragmas back from the connection
Open failures map to `DbError::Open { path, source }` and permission-tightening failures to `DbError::Permissions { path }`; neither message contains any cached data
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: `src/auth/file_source.rs` already has the `OWNER_READ_WRITE = 0o600` create-then-chmod pattern and `#[cfg(unix)]` guards — reuse that shape rather than inventing a new one. `src/config/paths.rs` tests show the env-var-driven tempdir helper to use instead of adding a `tempfile` dev-dependency. No schema/DDL here.

tasks.title: Schema DDL and idempotent migration runner
acceptance: `src/db/schema.sql` creates tables `projects`, `items`, `sections`, `labels`, `notes`, `filters`, `user`, `day_orders` and `meta` (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT), each resource table keyed by the Sync API `id` and carrying the columns the read queries need (`project_id`, `section_id`, `parent_id`, `child_order`, `checked`, `due_date`, `labels`, `content`, …) plus a `raw` JSON column for round-tripping fields not modelled as columns
Indices exist for at least `items(project_id, child_order)`, `items(section_id, child_order)`, `items(parent_id, child_order)`, `items(due_date)` and `items(checked)`
`migrations::run(&Connection) -> Result<i32>` applies all pending migrations in one transaction per migration and returns the resulting `user_version`
Running `run()` twice on the same database is a no-op the second time: same `user_version`, no error, no duplicate objects (unit test asserts schema object names/count unchanged)
A database whose `user_version` is greater than the compiled-in `SCHEMA_VERSION` fails with `DbError::UnsupportedSchemaVersion { found, supported }` instead of being migrated
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Use `PRAGMA user_version` as the version marker (no separate migrations table) and embed the DDL with `include_str!("schema.sql")`. Column set must cover the queries specified in T-308 — read that task before choosing columns. EPIC-05 will add a `commands` table as migration 2, so the runner must be a list of versioned steps, not a single blob.

tasks.title: meta table accessors for sync_token and sync timestamps
acceptance: `meta.rs` exposes get/set helpers for the keys `sync_token`, `last_sync_at` and `full_sync_date_utc`, each returning `Result<Option<String>>` on read
`sync_token()` returns `None` on a fresh database and the caller treats that as "needs full sync" (documented in rustdoc)
Writes are upserts (`INSERT .. ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE`): setting the same key twice leaves exactly one row (unit test)
Setters accept a `&Connection` so they can be called inside the T-307 apply transaction
A unit test writes a token, drops the connection, reopens the same file and reads the identical value back
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Sync tokens are not secrets but are user-scoped: never log their value, only their presence. Keep this module free of resource-table knowledge so EPIC-06 scheduling can depend on it alone.

tasks.title: Upsert/delete for projects, sections, labels, filters and user
acceptance: Each module exposes `upsert(&Connection, &T) -> Result<()>` and `delete(&Connection, &Id) -> Result<()>` for its `src/api/model` type
`upsert` is idempotent: applying the same resource twice leaves one row with identical column values (unit test per resource)
`upsert` of a changed resource overwrites every mapped column, including setting a column back to NULL when the model field is `None` (unit test on at least one nullable column)
The `raw` column stores the serde-serialised resource so unmodelled fields survive a round trip (unit test asserts a round-tripped JSON value is byte-equal after re-serialisation of the parsed model)
`user` is stored as a single-row table keyed on the user id; a second `upsert` with a different id replaces the row rather than adding one
rusqlite failures map to `DbError::Sqlite`, serde failures to `DbError::Decode`; no `unwrap`/`expect` in production code (clippy `unwrap_used`/`expect_used` are deny)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Consume the existing EPIC-03 model types from `src/api/model/` (`Project`, `Section`, `Label`, `Filter`, `User`, `Id`) — do not redefine them. Use prepared statements (`Connection::prepare_cached`) and named params. No transaction management here; T-307 owns the transaction boundary.

tasks.title: Upsert/delete for items, notes and day_orders
acceptance: `item::upsert` maps `project_id`, `section_id`, `parent_id`, `child_order`, `checked`, `priority`, `content`, `description`, the `due`/`deadline` objects (flattened `due_date` column plus the full object in `raw`) and `labels`
Items with `checked: true` are stored, not dropped (REQ-001 D3 retention); a unit test asserts a completed item is readable after upsert
`note::upsert` keys notes by id and records their `item_id`/`project_id` parent so notes can be fetched per task
`day_order::replace_all(&Connection, &serde_json::Map<String, Value>)` replaces the whole `day_orders` table contents in one statement batch (the Sync API sends the map wholesale)
`upsert` is idempotent and `delete` on a missing id is `Ok(())` (unit tests)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Models come from `src/api/model/item.rs` and `note.rs`; `day_orders` is a tolerant `serde_json::Map` on `SyncResponse` (see `src/api/sync.rs`) so keep the storage equally tolerant. Column names must match the schema agreed in T-303 — coordinate via `src/db/schema.sql`, do not add columns here.

tasks.title: Apply a SyncResponse delta in a single transaction
acceptance: `apply_sync(&mut Connection, &SyncResponse) -> Result<ApplyStats>` applies every resource list plus `sync_token`, `last_sync_at` and `full_sync_date_utc` inside one rusqlite transaction
Resources with `is_deleted: true` are removed from their table; all others are upserted (unit test covers both in one response)
When `full_sync_date_utc` is present (full sync) the resource tables are cleared before the upserts, so stale rows absent from a full sync do not survive (unit test)
An incremental response leaves rows it does not mention untouched (unit test)

A failure part-way through (e.g. an item whose payload fails to encode) rolls back the whole transaction: `sync_token` and every row are exactly as before the call, asserted by a unit test that injects a bad resource
`ApplyStats` reports per-resource upsert/delete counts and is `Debug`-printable without any task content
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: `SyncResponse` lives in `src/api/sync.rs` (full-sync marker is `full_sync_date_utc`). All row writes go through the T-305/T-306 helpers — this task adds no SQL of its own except the full-sync table clears. Keep it synchronous (rusqlite is blocking); EPIC-06 decides the off-thread execution.

tasks.title: Read queries for the TUI views
acceptance: `queries.rs` exposes `items_by_project`, `items_by_section`, `subtasks_of`, `today`, `upcoming { days }`, `items_by_label` and `inbox`, each returning `Result<Vec<Item>>`
Every result set is ordered by `child_order` ascending, with a deterministic tiebreak on `id` (unit test with equal `child_order` values)
`today` returns items whose `due_date` is today or earlier (overdue included) and excludes `checked` items; `upcoming { days }` returns the next N days excluding today, also excluding `checked` items
`inbox` resolves the inbox project via the user's `inbox_project_id` and returns `Ok(vec![])` (not an error) when no user row is cached
Each query reconstructs a full `Item` from the stored `raw` payload so no field is lost in the round trip (unit test compares an upserted item to the queried one for equality)
A `checked: true` item is excluded from the view queries but still retrievable by `item_by_id` (REQ-001 D3)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Queries must be index-covered against the indices created in T-303 — if a query needs an index that does not exist, stop and flag it rather than editing `schema.sql` from here. Date handling: `due_date` is stored as the Sync API `YYYY-MM-DD` string prefix so comparisons are lexicographic; take "today" as a parameter so tests are not wall-clock dependent.

tasks.title: SqliteCacheWipe: real delete_all wired into logout
acceptance: `SqliteCacheWipe` implements the existing `crate::auth::cache_wipe::CacheWipe` trait with `describe() == "cache"`
`wipe()` removes the cache database file (and its `-wal`/`-shm` siblings) and is idempotent: calling it when the file is absent returns `Ok(())`
After a wipe, opening the database again creates a fresh file with schema version `SCHEMA_VERSION`, zero rows and no `sync_token` (unit test)
`src/cli/logout.rs` passes `SqliteCacheWipe` instead of `NoopCacheWipe`; existing logout tests still pass and the user-facing summary line now says `cache`
`NoopCacheWipe` remains in `src/auth/cache_wipe.rs` for tests — this task does not modify that file
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: The seam is already in place from T-108: read `src/auth/cache_wipe.rs` and the `run_logout_with(...)` injection point in `src/cli/logout.rs`. Keep the trait definition untouched; only the concrete impl and the wiring change.

tasks.title: Integration test: full then incremental fixture apply
acceptance: `tests/fixtures/sync_incremental.json` is a hand-written incremental Sync API response containing one updated item, one `is_deleted: true` item and one new item, all referencing ids present in the existing `tests/fixtures/sync_full.json`

The test applies `sync_full.json` then `sync_incremental.json` to a temp database and asserts the exact final row set: updated item has the new content, deleted item is absent, new item present, untouched items unchanged
A test asserts `sync_token` round-trips across process restart semantics: write, drop the connection, reopen the same path, read the same token back
A test applies a malformed delta (fixture mutated in-test into an invalid payload) and asserts the database is byte-for-row identical to the pre-call state
A test asserts the view queries (`today`, `items_by_project`) return the expected ids and order after the two applies
All fixture data is fake: no real token, user id, email or personal content
`cargo test --all` passes
tasks.context: `tests/sync_fixture.rs` (T-208) already shows the fixture-loading pattern and the existing `tests/fixtures/sync_full.json`. Create the temp DB with a test-local temp dir helper (no `tempfile` dev-dependency is present; follow the helper style used in `src/config/paths.rs` tests).

tasks.title: Integration test: 5k-item query performance bound
acceptance: The test seeds a temp database with 5,000 generated items spread over 25 projects with varied `due_date` and `child_order` values
`today` and `items_by_project` are each executed after a warm-up run and the median of 5 runs is asserted to be under 50ms
The seeding phase is excluded from the measured time
A failure message reports the measured duration so a regression is diagnosable from CI logs
The test asserts both queries return a non-empty, correctly ordered result so a trivially-empty fast path cannot pass it

`cargo test --all` passes (the test is `--release`-independent; if debug-build timings are too noisy, document the chosen bound and `#[ignore]` policy in the test header instead of silently loosening it)
tasks.context: This guards the EPIC-04 acceptance bullet "5k items: today / project tasks query each <50ms". Generated data only — no real task content. If the bound cannot be met in a debug build, report back rather than deleting the assertion (hard rule 9).

tasks.title: Integration test: checked-item retention lifetime
acceptance: A test applies a delta containing an item transitioning to `checked: true` and asserts the row remains in the cache with `checked = 1`
The checked item is absent from `today`/`items_by_project` results but returned by `item_by_id`, proving `uncomplete` (FR-27, EPIC-08) can still read it
A test asserts a checked item is only removed when a later delta marks it `is_deleted: true`, not by the mere act of completing it
A test asserts a full sync that no longer lists the checked item does drop it (full-sync replace semantics), documenting the retention window in the test header
`cargo test --all` passes
tasks.context: Verification task for REQ-001 D3 (open question 3): v1 keeps `checked: true` items in cache so recent completions can be undone. Fixtures are in-test JSON literals; keep them fake.

tasks.title: Document the cache schema, apply semantics and wipe
acceptance: Documents the database location per platform, the `0600` permission guarantee and the WAL/foreign-keys pragmas
Lists every table and index with a one-line purpose, and states the current `SCHEMA_VERSION` plus how to add migration N+1
Explains delta-apply semantics: single transaction, upsert vs `is_deleted`, full-sync replace, rollback on failure
Documents the read queries available to the TUI, their ordering guarantee and the checked-item retention rule (REQ-001 D3)
Documents `logout` cache wipe behaviour and what a user loses by it
Records the open question on `child_order` / `day_orders` ordering semantics as unverified against real data
No real tokens, user ids or personal data appear in any example
tasks.context: Follow the structure of `docs/manual/epic-03-sync-api.md` (T-210). Documentation only — no code or schema changes in this task.
